sections.h2: Is an Amarillo house taxed by Potter County or Randall County?
sections.html:
Either, depending on where the parcel sits, because Amarillo straddles the county line. Each county has its own tax assessor-collector, but one office values property for both: the Potter-Randall Appraisal District.

The Comptroller's county directories name the units that can show up on an Amarillo bill: the City of Amarillo, Amarillo Independent School District, Amarillo Junior College District, the county, and in some addresses Bushland ISD, River Road ISD, Highland Park ISD, Canyon ISD or High Plains Underground Water Conservation District No. 1.

  • Potter County Tax Assessor-Collector: 900 S. Polk St., Suite 106, Amarillo, 806-342-2600, mail to P.O. Box 2289, Amarillo 79105-2289.
  • Randall County Tax Assessor-Collector: 501 16th St., Suite 200, Canyon, 806-468-5540, mail to P.O. Box 997, Canyon 79015-0997.
  • Potter-Randall Appraisal District: 5701 Hollywood Rd., Amarillo, 806-358-1601, for values, exemptions and protests in both counties.

sections.h2: What tax rate did Amarillo set for 2026/2027?
sections.html:
The city's budget news page gives a total of $0.43070 per $100 of valuation: $0.32412 for maintenance and operations and $0.10658 for existing debt. Council approved the 2026/2027 budget with that rate by a 4-1 vote at a special meeting in late September 2026.

The city says the budget brings in $2,063,963 more property tax revenue than the year before, a 2.58 percent rise, and that $1,295,675 of the increase comes from newly added property. It describes the maintenance and operations rate as effectively 2.9 percent higher, which it equates to about $9 on a $100,000 home.

The same news release charts what Amarillo returns through economic development agreements. Property tax rebates run under Chapter 311 and Chapter 380 deals, and the city also reports hotel occupancy tax and sales tax rebates. Separately, Chapter 312 abatements reduced taxes by $1,143,899 at the city level in 2024/2025, within $2,959,496 abated by all participating entities.

sections.h2: When are Amarillo property taxes due, and what happens after?
sections.html:
Bills go out near October 1 and are payable through January 31. February 1 brings a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest, and the penalty adds a point each month until it hits 12 percent on July 1. Attorney-contract units may tack on up to 20 percent.

Homeowners 65 or older, disabled owners and disabled veterans can pay a homestead bill in installments, and some collectors offer plans stretching to 36 months. A written request to waive penalty and interest must come before day 181 after delinquency, with prompt payment. Call the Potter or Randall office before January 31 if you expect to fall short.

sections.h2: How does the Potter-Randall Appraisal District help owners with exemptions?
sections.html:
Its website runs an online homestead and over-65 portal, a notice-of-estimated-taxes page with a registration option for alerts, and a login portal where owners can see valuations and file appeals or exemptions. A 2026 Disaster Declaration and Exemption item sits at the top of the news feed, and the home page also publishes a 7.75% basic capitalization rate for 2026 low-income housing valuations.

The state's headline numbers are $140,000 off the school tax base for a homestead and $60,000 more for owners 65 or older or disabled. Local governments may add up to 20 percent, so ask which options Amarillo, Potter County, Randall County and Amarillo Junior College District use. Veterans with disability ratings qualify on a sliding scale, up to the whole homestead at 100 percent.

  • Apply before May 1 in general; some veteran claims can wait up to five years after delinquency.
  • Heirs with no deed in their name can claim with an affidavit of ownership interest, a death certificate and a recent utility bill.

sections.h2: How can an Amarillo owner protest an appraised value?
sections.html:
Send a written protest to the appraisal district by May 15 or 30 days after the notice, whichever is later. Homestead notices start around April 1 and review board hearings begin about mid-May. The board can change only market value, never rates. Further appeals go to district court, arbitration or, over $1,000,000, the State Office of Administrative Hearings.

The district serves both counties, so one filing covers a parcel on either side of the line. Pay the undisputed amount to the Potter or Randall collector before delinquency while the protest is pending.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Amarillo households?
sections.html: The July 2025 estimate is 205,130 residents on 102.30 land square miles, up from 200,393 in 2020. Owners occupy about 59.7 percent of homes, valued at a median of $196,900, and the median household earns $65,912. The city counts 79,741 households and 10,973 veterans, and its 2022 retail sales reached $5,722,271 thousand.

sections.h2: How does a tax lien affect an Amarillo sale?
sections.html: The lien is created January 1 and stays with the parcel, and the January 1 owner remains personally liable after a sale. Title stays clouded until the taxes are paid. An owner with accounts in both counties, for instance on adjoining parcels, should ask each tax office for a separate payoff letter before closing.

sections.h2: What happens when an Amarillo house goes to a tax sale?
sections.html: Taxing units can foreclose and sell through the constable or an agent. Texas keeps no statewide calendar, so watch the Potter and Randall county sites and clerk postings. A former owner can redeem a homestead for two years after the purchaser's deed is filed by paying the price plus a premium of 25 percent in year one or 50 percent in year two, along with costs. Other property has a 180-day window. Surplus money belongs to the former owner for two years.

faqs.q: Is Amarillo in Potter County or Randall County?
faqs.a: Both. The city lies across the two counties, so the bill comes from the county where the parcel sits. The Potter-Randall Appraisal District values property in both.

faqs.q: What is the Amarillo city tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The total on the city's budget news page is $0.43070 per $100 of valuation: $0.32412 for maintenance and operations and $0.10658 for debt.

faqs.q: When do Amarillo property taxes go delinquent?
faqs.a: February 1, after a January 31 due date. A 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest attach at once, and the penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1.

faqs.q: Who do I call to pay Amarillo property taxes?
faqs.a: Call the county office for your parcel: Potter County at 806-342-2600 or Randall County at 806-468-5540. Use the Potter-Randall Appraisal District at 806-358-1601 for value and exemption questions.

faqs.q: How large is the homestead exemption in Amarillo?
faqs.a: State law removes $140,000 of homestead value from the school tax base, plus $60,000 for owners 65 or older or disabled. Cities and counties may add local exemptions of up to 20 percent.
